svg.title: Multiplicative transformations stretch and reflect
svg.desc: Three curves sharing a vertex at the origin. The solid one is the parent, one half x squared. One dashed curve is its mirror image below the horizontal axis, which is the parent multiplied by minus one: a vertical dilation with a reflection. The other dashed curve is much narrower than the parent, which is the parent with its input multiplied by two: a horizontal dilation by a factor of one half. A factor applied to the output scales the graph by that factor; a factor applied to the input scales it by the RECIPROCAL, so multiplying the input by two makes the graph half as wide, not twice as wide.
svg.text: a f(x) scales vertically; f(bx) scales horizontally by 1/b
Inside the function, the factor acts as its RECIPROCAL.
